add.issue.name: Create an isolated synthetic build/test fixture

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md, evidence stage 1A; docs/architecture.md.

Create a small nonproprietary fixture with a real build and test, a declared mise toolchain, staged/unstaged/untracked changes, and absolute/relative linked-worktree layouts. Choose the smallest suitable language during implementation.

Acceptance:
- Runs in fresh temporary storage with unique resource names; never uses personal or employer repositories as test fixtures.
- Records source bytes, index/tree, HEAD/branch and full Git status for later persistence comparisons.
- Cleanup is limited to resources created by this fixture.

Ready to start. No Argus inputs required; fixture success alone cannot close Milestone 1.

add.issue.name: Build the minimal verified OS and mise image

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Implement one canonical Dockerfile with a minimal non-root base and mise. Choose and record supported base/tool versions using primary sources and architecture-specific integrity verification.

Acceptance:
- Build on the available Apple Silicon host; record actual image architecture, identity, versions, integrity checks and cold-build time.
- Start a shell and inspect installed tools without startup downloads or upgrades.
- Exclude GUI, agent supervisor, host socket and credentials from the default base.
- A failed download/build does not replace a working image or modify source/state.

Covers M1-01 and build failures in M1-09. Ready to start.

add.issue.name: Add the fixture toolchain as a declared image layer

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Install synthetic project tools through mise and a shared Dockerfile stage during explicit builds. Keep application lockfiles authoritative and installed tools outside persistent state mounts.

Acceptance: real fixture build/tests pass with recorded versions; startup performs no installation/upgrade; hooks/tasks require deliberate trust; missing tools fail clearly. Preserve one build path for optional interfaces. Covers M1-01, M1-09.

Depends on: 61Q7E8F (Build the minimal verified OS and mise image); SKSJTMN (Create an isolated synthetic build/test fixture).

add.issue.name: Derive stable workspace identity from canonical checkout paths

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Implement a minimal helper for bounded hestia-<label>-<hash> workspace IDs from canonical checkout paths; derive repo-group identity from the common Git directory. Document hash choice.

Acceptance: matching basenames at different paths and worktrees have distinct IDs; branch/agent/variant changes preserve ID; symlink aliases match; full-path mismatch/collision fails before reuse; moved checkouts get new IDs while old state survives. Names fit Compose constraints, with no global container names. Covers M1-04, M1-09. Ready to start.

add.issue.name: Plan scoped host source and linked-worktree mounts

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Discover checkout/common Git metadata through Git and preserve resolved host paths inside the container. Use Compose and minimal helpers.

Acceptance: inspectable mounts expose only selected source, required metadata and explicit state/access; no broad home/repos mounts, sibling source or Docker socket. Host/container edits and Git status/diff agree. Stage/diff supported absolute/relative worktree layouts without rewriting pointers. Missing paths, inaccessible metadata and unsupported layouts fail clearly without mutation. Covers M1-02, M1-05, M1-09. Full concurrency follows later.

Depends on: 503RD0P (Derive stable workspace identity from canonical checkout paths); SKSJTMN (Create an isolated synthetic build/test fixture).

add.issue.name: Establish non-root writes and separate Linux build artifacts

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Choose effective ownership for the tested macOS runtime; copying host UID is not proof. Map Linux dependency/build outputs to workspace caches, separate from durable agent state.

Acceptance: real non-root writes succeed on source/state/cache mounts; no recursive host chown or unexpected ownership changes; native and Linux artifacts cannot overwrite each other; unwritable state gives actionable recovery. Classify caches versus durable data; mounts do not hide installed tools. Covers M1-03, M1-09.

Depends on: 61Q7E8F (Build the minimal verified OS and mise image); WGHQ2GW (Add the fixture toolchain as a declared image layer); JP73P2D (Plan scoped host source and linked-worktree mounts).

add.issue.name: Provide scoped Compose start, attach, stop and recreation

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Implement/document inspect/validate, start, attach, stop, remove-runtime and explicit rebuild through Compose and minimal helpers, using workspace-scoped resources.

Acceptance: validate paths, identity, tools, writes and published-port conflicts; attach to existing workspace; routine stop/removal/rebuild preserves source, Git and durable state/volumes. Finish active work before rebuild; replacement gets a different container ID. No routine down -v, global prune, destructive reset or source deletion. Document recovery/offline-startup limits. Covers M1-06, M1-09. No custom CLI.

Depends on: JP73P2D (Plan scoped host source and linked-worktree mounts); KSCDG1J (Establish non-root writes and separate Linux build artifacts).

add.issue.name: Select the first terminal agent and approved authentication flow

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Human decision: choose Codex CLI, omp or pi.dev based on workflow preference, employer approval, provider access and native session portability. One integration keeps the proof small; an all-agent matrix delays it.

Acceptance: record one agent and permitted provider/auth flow without credentials/internal endpoints; identify native state/session/credential paths and login/refresh/resume behavior from primary sources; note differing personal/employer constraints. Blocks agent integration, not base/toolchain/identity work.

add.issue.comment.md: Blocked: awaiting the user's first-agent selection and permitted provider/auth approach. Foundation image, toolchain and identity work can proceed.

edit.description.md:
Source: docs/milestone-1.md and docs/architecture.md.

Confirm work laptop OS/CPU and approved runtime; inspect Argus toolchain, build/test commands, services and networking there. Keep employer code/configuration and detailed evidence there.

Acceptance: employer-local inputs define executable build/test and required access/services; share only sanitized constraints/readiness appropriate for Hestia. If Windows/WSL2, validate the pilot during M1B now. Use the employer-approved runtime; discuss alternatives only if none is usable. Does not block the personal synthetic fixture.

add.issue.name: Integrate one native terminal agent with durable private state

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Add only the selected agent as an optional shared image layer, invoked directly with its native permissions and sessions. Scope persistent state by workspace and agent, outside source/build context; document sensitivity and supported native login/refresh/logout/resume behavior. Configure Git authentication separately.

Acceptance: real provider login and agent-assisted fixture change; recreation resumes saved session or documented native equivalent. Missing/expired auth leaves shell/source usable with recovery instructions. Credentials do not enter images, tracked/generated Compose or logs; logout preserves unrelated work. No shared writable agent home, broad credential mounts or replacement permission engine. Covers M1-07 and M1-09.

Depends on: TG7VZBV (Select the first terminal agent and approved authentication flow); 24GJSHY (Provide scoped Compose start, attach, stop and recreation).

add.issue.name: Clear only a disposable fixture workspace's classified caches

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Provide/document explicit cache clearing scoped to one synthetic workspace's classified recoverable storage.

Acceptance: before/after snapshots show source bytes, Git/index/untracked work and durable agent state unchanged; dependency/build caches regenerate and real build/tests pass. Use unique disposable resources and verify target identity before removal. Reject durable/mixed-state targets; no global prune or production resource IDs. Covers M1-08; destructive state reset automation remains deferred.

Depends on: KSCDG1J (Establish non-root writes and separate Linux build artifacts); 24GJSHY (Provide scoped Compose start, attach, stop and recreation).

add.issue.name: Run and record the complete Apple Silicon recreation proof

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Execute the M1A journey with meaningful isolated integration checks, covering M1-01 through M1-09. Use actual file writes, Git operations and real build/tests, plus failure cases required by the spec.

Acceptance: finish active work, snapshot source bytes, index/tree, branch/HEAD, status/untracked files and selected agent state; remove/recreate with a new container ID; compare before resumed work with zero unintended durable changes. Resume the agent and rerun build/tests. Record platform/runtime/tool versions, image/container IDs, commands, exit codes, integrity evidence and cold/warm timings. Every requirement is pass/fail/not run with evidence. Synthetic auth is not provider proof; fixture success does not close Argus acceptance.

Depends on: SKSJTMN (Create an isolated synthetic build/test fixture); WGHQ2GW (Add the fixture toolchain as a declared image layer); 503RD0P (Derive stable workspace identity from canonical checkout paths); JP73P2D (Plan scoped host source and linked-worktree mounts); KSCDG1J (Establish non-root writes and separate Linux build artifacts); 24GJSHY (Provide scoped Compose start, attach, stop and recreation); XJVWF4K (Integrate one native terminal agent with durable private state); HE2GM6N (Clear only a disposable fixture workspace's classified caches).

add.issue.name: Complete the employer-local Argus workflow and recreation proof

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

On the work laptop, configure the agreed workspace for Argus using its existing build/test workflow and required services. Keep source, credentials, employer configuration and detailed evidence there.

Acceptance: a real agent-assisted reviewable change builds/tests successfully; finish active work and snapshot source/Git/selected state; recreate with a new container ID, compare durable state before resume, resume session and pass build/tests again. Record sanitized outcomes/limitations appropriate for Hestia. Include Windows/WSL2 here if that is the pilot platform. Close M1 only when combined fixture and Argus evidence covers all nine requirements; publishing the Argus change is not required.

add.issue.name: Prove isolation of two concurrent repositories

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Run two nonproprietary repositories concurrently through the canonical build, including matching directory basenames. Each must build/test.

Acceptance: identities, source/state/cache/service resources remain distinct; declared ports are usable or conflicts rejected clearly; no unintended sharing. Capture effective mounts/resources and actual operations. Keep this proof independent from the worktree-sharing case. Source: docs/roadmap.md, Milestone 2.

Depends on: E66EJET (Complete the employer-local Argus workflow and recreation proof).

add.issue.name: Prove recreating one project leaves its neighbor usable

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Extend the concurrent-project fixture with dirty work and selected state in both repositories. Recreate only one workspace while the other performs useful build/test work.

Acceptance: the recreated container ID changes; both durable snapshots remain correct; the neighbor remains usable and retains its work/state/resources. Cleanup touches only test-owned resources. Source: docs/roadmap.md, Milestone 2.

Depends on: CF62H3E (Prove isolation of two concurrent repositories).

add.issue.name: Prove concurrent agent workflows across linked Git worktrees

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Run the main checkout and a linked worktree in separate workspaces through terminal agents on different intended branches. Exercise real edits and build/tests, then recreate one workspace.

Acceptance: both retain their work and selected state; Git stage/diff and common metadata still resolve; no branch/state confusion or broad host-home mount. Document shared-metadata limits rather than claiming a security boundary between worktrees. Source: docs/roadmap.md, Milestone 3.

Depends on: 3B36AE6 (Prove recreating one project leaves its neighbor usable); JP73P2D (Plan scoped host source and linked-worktree mounts).

add.issue.name: Define and capture the durable workspace backup set

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Define a minimal backup manifest for source, Git/common worktree metadata, selected agent sessions and service data. Capture a consistent fixture backup after active work is stopped or quiesced using supported service mechanisms.

Acceptance: explicit inclusions/exclusions and sensitivity classification; caches excluded; credentials handled explicitly with reauthentication preferred and encrypted handling for unavoidable mixed state. No silent host credential-tree copying. Include enough path/identity metadata for validated relocation. A backup file alone is not restore proof. Source: architecture storage/auth ADRs and roadmap Milestone 4.

Depends on: M9FMY5V (Prove concurrent agent workflows across linked Git worktrees).

add.issue.name: Restore a fixture workspace into fresh storage and verify it

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Restore the backup into fresh isolated storage. Validate relocated checkout identity and Git/worktree relationships explicitly; do not silently reuse mismatched state.

Acceptance: saved source/index/untracked work and selected agent/service state match; Git/worktree operations succeed; reauthenticate where required; rebuild excluded caches and pass actual build/tests. Record commands, snapshots and limits without secrets. Source: docs/roadmap.md, Milestone 4.

Depends on: B6J27FG (Define and capture the durable workspace backup set).

add.issue.name: Run the acceptance suite on a real Windows WSL2 host

edit.description.md:
Source of scope: docs/milestone-1.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md. Planned work; no runtime acceptance is complete.

Expand any Windows evidence already gathered during Argus using the same canonical Dockerfile/build definition. Prefer source in the WSL Linux filesystem; record actual source placement.

Acceptance: run single-repo, concurrent-project, linked-worktree and backup/restore proofs; record Windows/WSL/runtime/CPU, permissions, path behavior and architecture-specific artifact verification. Report individual pass/fail/not-run results and support only for exercised combinations. Fixes discovered become small follow-up tickets. Do not create a platform fork or delay a Windows Argus pilot until this milestone. Source: docs/roadmap.md, Milestone 5.

Depends on: R3N7X5F (Restore a fixture workspace into fresh storage and verify it).
